title: Hepatoprotective and neuroprotective effects of quinacrine against bile duct ligation-induced hepatic encephalopathy in

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – behavioral testing timeline (section beginning "At the completion of the experiment on day 28...")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states "At the completion of the experiment on day 28, the animals underwent behavioral assessments on day 29 and day 30", but the same Methods section describes MWM training "for a duration of four days (from day 25 to 28)", NOR habituation "on day 26 and 27" and NOR training "on day 28". Behavioral testing therefore began on day 25, not after day 28, so the stated timeline contradicts the detailed protocols.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – MWM probe test and NOR test
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The MWM probe trial ("During the fifth day, which was day 29, a probing test was carried out") and the NOR test ("On the 29th day (test day), the animals were reintroduced inside the test box") are scheduled on the same day. Performing a 2-min forced-swim probe trial and an object-recognition memory test on the same animals on the same day confounds the recognition memory measure (stress, fatigue, wet animals) and is not a valid protocol as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – serum biochemistry (ALP and ALT kits)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: ALP is said to be measured with a kit "provided by BioAssay Systems in Hayward, CA, USA ... (catalogue No. A526)", while ALT is measured with "TECO DIAGNOSTICS ... (catalogue No. A561 and A526, respectively)". The identical catalogue number A526 is attributed to two different manufacturers and two different analytes; A526 is a TECO ALT kit, so the ALP kit/catalogue attribution is incorrect.

Serum total ammonia values are said to be "expressed as mmol/ml", i.e. mol/L. Physiological ammonia concentrations are in the µmol/L range (~10^-6 mol/L); the stated unit is six orders of magnitude off and cannot be correct for the Abcam ab83360 assay.

Reduced glutathione in liver/hippocampus is reported in "pg/mg protein". Tissue GSH is normally in the nmol/mg protein (µg/mg) range; expressing it in pg/mg protein is off by roughly six orders of magnitude and inconsistent with the MDA units (nmol/mg protein) reported in the same sentence.

With α = 0.05, power = 0.85, effect size f = 0.5 and 5 groups, G*Power returns a required total sample of ~55 (11 per group), not 60. The claim that "A total sample size of 60 animals (12 each group) was established based on these criteria" is not reproducible from the stated parameters (and the statistical test used in the computation is not specified).

The text states "hippocampi were dissected from brain tissues, then hippocampal as well as liver tissues of each sample were submerged in liquid nitrogen" and then "For histological examination, whole brains as well as liver tissues of each sample ... were preserved in ... formalin". The same brain cannot simultaneously have its hippocampi dissected and frozen and be preserved whole for histology; the allocation of tissues per animal is internally contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – ELISA description (IL-6, TNF-α, NF-κB, hydroxyproline)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The procedure described ("coating the wells of the ELISA plates with the samples and incubating them overnight at 4°C" followed by addition of "enzyme-conjugated antibodies specific to IL-6 and TNF-α") is a direct/indirect ELISA on sample-coated plates, which is not how the cited commercial pre-coated sandwich ELISA kits work and contradicts the statement that the manufacturer's instructions were followed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – novel object recognition discrimination index
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The discrimination index is defined as "the difference in the amount of time consumed examining familiar and novel things, divided by the overall exploration time". As written (familiar − novel), the index would be negative for intact recognition memory; the standard definition is (novel − familiar)/total exploration time.

The BDL-only group received no daily intraperitoneal vehicle injections while the quinacrine groups received 28 daily i.p. injections of drug in distilled water. Without a BDL + vehicle group, the handling/injection stress is uncontrolled, so differences between BDL and BDL/quinacrine cannot be attributed solely to quinacrine.

The GFAP primary antibody listed (Thermo Cat. No. 13-0300) is a rat monoclonal, yet the detection system described is the DAKO EnVision HRP-conjugated secondary (anti-mouse/anti-rabbit). As described, the secondary reagent would not detect the stated primary antibody.

Tissue homogenate protein is first said to be measured with "the Bradford assay kit, Abcam ... (catalogue No. ab102535)", while the Western blot section states lysate protein was "tested with the Bradford Protein Assay Kit (SK3041) from BIO BASIC INC, Canada". Two different kits are reported for the same measurement without explanation.

The claim that "BMP2 can effectively counteract the fibrotic effects of TGF-β1, thereby mitigating the progression of fibrosis [8]" misrepresents the hepatic fibrosis literature, where BMP7 (not BMP2) is the recognized TGF-β1 antagonist and BMP2 has been repeatedly reported as pro-fibrogenic in hepatic stellate cells; the attribution appears to conflate BMP2 with BMP7.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – anesthesia for bile duct ligation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: "Ketamine (90 mg/kg/i.p.) was used to put the rats under anesthesia" as the sole agent for laparotomy. Ketamine alone does not provide surgical-plane anesthesia/analgesia in rats (it requires combination with xylazine or similar), so the described anesthetic protocol is inadequate/implausible for an abdominal survival surgery.

A total Smad1/5/8 antibody is listed among the primary antibodies, but the quantification section states band intensities were normalized to beta-actin only. Phospho-Smad1/5/8 must be normalized to total Smad1/5/8 to support the claims about BMP-Smad activation; the stated analysis does not use the total Smad data that was reportedly generated.
"Male Wistar rats, 12 weeks old, 200–250 g" is internally inconsistent: male Wistar rats at 12 weeks of age typically weigh 300–400 g; the stated weight corresponds to roughly 7–8 weeks of age.
